messages:
Riley: quick heads-up, ran a set of steady-state profiles on TP4xPP2 (8xA100) with KV cache enabled. seeing large p99 token lat spikes and all-reduce time ballooning.

Priya: numbers? config? warmup or steady-state?

Riley: steady-state. seq=512, micro-batch=1, model ~7B, prefix KV caching on. nvprof + perf traces collected.

Riley: short perf summary (5-run avg):
``
throughput: 620 tok/s (baseline ~840)
p50 token: 18ms (baseline 12ms)
p99 token: 95ms (baseline 42ms)
all-reduce per-step: 7.9ms (baseline 2.3ms)
comm/compute overlap down ~65%
```

Jun: yikes. what's the message size distribution over NCCL?

Riley: surprisingly small due to KV-sharding + our chunker. typical per-GPU payloads ~48KB, with many fragments ~8KB. fragmentation shows in nccl traces.

Theo: that smells like ring inefficiency on tiny messages. tree topologies usually cut latency for small reductions. which algorithm did NCCL pick?

Riley: default selector picked ring. I forced tree in a quick experiment + forced small-reduce kernel (k_reduce_small). results: p99 down to ~50ms, throughput up to 770 tok/s.

Priya: did you isolate kernel launch overhead vs comm path? small kernels + launch overhead can matter with micro-batch=1.

Riley: yes 12 when using k_reduce_small we saw ~1.3ms step improvement independent of the comm switch. combined with tree it was best.

perf-bot: flamegraph uploaded -> https://perf.example.company/redwood/1777777777/flame

Jun: another lever is coalescing in the batcher. With micro-batch=1 a short hold (1-2ms) might aggregate fragments into larger payloads and make ring cheaper. did you try a coalesce window?

Riley: tried 1.5ms coalesce: average message grew to ~48KB and performance was close to the tree+kernel path. downside: slight tail increase on cold prefixes.

Theo: So two practical mitigations: (A) topology-aware selector prefer tree for <64KB messages + switch to small-msg kernel, (B) a tiny coalesce window in the batcher to merge fragmented KV writes. both low-risk.

Priya: agree. also add metrics so we detect regressions: message_size_histogram (per-step) + kernel_choice label. If chunker changes we should alert.

Riley: sketched heuristic: if avg_msg_size < 64KB and topology_locality_score high -> prefer tree; else ring. will add as PR.

Riley: PR draft: https://git.example.company/r/inference/+/PR-2486 (selector + k_reduce_small integration + test harness)

Jun: add a synthetic test that mimics KV fragmentation (variable chunk sizes, many tiny shards) and assert p99 and all-reduce time bounds.

Priya: I'll build that test and a regression case. also suggest a node-level flag so Dedicated can opt-in to canary.

Theo: rollout plan: enable heuristic behind canary flag for a subset of TP workloads, monitor p99 token latency and all-reduce time.

Riley: planned next steps in-thread:
- PR review + benchmark (Riley) : 2d
- message_size_histogram metric + dashboard (Jun) : 1d
- synthetic KV fragmentation regression test (Priya) : 2d
- canary flag + canary dashboard (Theo) : 1d

Priya: sounds good. thanks for the repro and numbers. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary created: canary/tp-tree-heuristic @ 1777777890

Riley: ping @eng-runtime in case others hit similar p99 spikes. I'll update the PR with the reproducible run script and exact perf harness commands.
